findings.text: follow-on: every PID record emitted by the second pass is keyed to a catalogue data name through dname_by_pid.get(pid, ""), whose fallback is an empty string. If a PID in the eddbreadOne readback is not present in the category's O-class list, source_dname lands as "" and the scanner builds accessor eddbreadOne(pid), which the census records as irc 1031 (an empty or invalid data name is exactly the failure mode the plan opened with). It does not manifest in the delivered data: all 58 PID rows in the live graph carry a non-empty data name in their accessor, so the mapping covered every returned PID for E101173. The path is a latent robustness gap for categories or shots where the readback returns a PID the table does not list, and carries no test.

justifications.durability: The change carries an executable guard: two tests in TestEdasPidKeyedGroup assert the PID row maps pid and data_class one_point, and the empty-PID row keeps pid unset. I reproduced the declared negative control independently, in a scratch overlay at /tmp/pidnc-review with pid forced to '' for pid_keyed rows: exactly TestEdasPidKeyedGroup::test_pid_keyed_rows_map_pid_and_one_point failed (1 failed, 5 passed, exit 1), so the test is a real fence and not a tautology. The one carried gap is the empty-source_dname fallback at enumerate_edas.py:186, which would yield a irc-ic 1031 accessor for a readback PID absent from the table and is untested; it does not manifest in the delivered data but it is a genuine latent path.
justifications.evidence: The headline figures reproduce independently and far from the manifest: total 6298, with_pid 58, bad_format 0, pid_one_point 58, class totals 5947/351 (5889 base + 58, unchanged nulls), and all 58 rows resolve a non-empty data name in their accessor. Both gate arms reproduce (59 baseline, 61 head, both exit 0), and the negative control reproduces the declared failing id. Two qualifications keep this off the ceiling: the reviewed manifest stores baseline_suite/after_suite as prose with no baseline log file (I produced one myself, so the numbers are now backed, but the reviewed run's own record did not carry the log); and I did not re-probe nakasvr26 to re-observe the eddbreadOne/eddbreadPara irc codes first-hand, so the call-shape answer rests on the run's census doc, the probe record and the graph outcome rather than my own remote measurement.
justifications.fit: The node extends the two owners the plan names — the existing EDAS scanner and its remote enumerate_edas.py — with a second pass and one branch. It introduces no sibling scanner, no new signal-id format, no new graph property or owner, and no abstraction; the uid scheme reuses 'facility:general/<cat>_<token>'. The PID is placed on the existing FacilitySignal.pid slot the scanner already wrote.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §3(c) is met end to end and independently reproduced: the one-point and condition data of E101173 keyed by PID No. is in the live graph as its own group: 58 FacilitySignal rows with pid set, all nine characters (four digits then five), all data_class one_point, each with an accessor carrying both the source data name and the PID, produced by the existing EDAS scanner's new pass. The scan took the graph 6240 -> 6298 with no existing row altered, and the open question is answered by the run (eddbreadOne with an empty PID enumerates the block; eddbreadPara returns irc 1014).
